drawn-indicator-fails-forced-colors-or-a.mechanism: Each delivery seat is a custom div[tabindex="0"][role="button"].seat whose only focus cue is a background-color swap on :focus (#f3f5f9 resting -> #ffe08a focused) after outline:none, with no border/box-shadow/outline change. In forced-colors mode the UA overrides author background-color with the system Canvas, so the amber tint collapses to the same colour as the unfocused seats; and because the seats are non-native div[tabindex] widgets, Chromium does not re-apply a UA forced-colors focus ring (it only does so for native input/select/button), leaving no fallback indicator.
drawn-indicator-fails-forced-colors-or-a.scenario: Coastliner rail booking seat picker whose custom div[role=button] seats signal focus only by a background-COLOR swap (#f3f5f9 -> #ffe08a) after outline:none; in forced-colors the tint collapses to system Canvas and, being a non-native widget, the seat gets no UA fallback ring, so the focused seat is pixel-identical to its neighbours.
drawn-indicator-fails-forced-colors-or-a.note: Scenario/mechanism described a different concrete page than the HTML: prose said a 'TidalSync backup preferences' dark-theme settings panel with text inputs, a select, and a Save button whose focus cue was a dashed-ring SVG background-IMAGE (data: URI), with primarySelector 'input[type=text]:focus, select:focus, button.save:focus'. The actual page is a Coastliner seat picker using custom div[role=button] seats whose cue is a background-COLOR swap (primarySelector .seat:focus) - none of those elements/selectors exist on the page. Same aspect (custom-drawn indicator lost in forced-colors / untrackable by AT), different concrete instance; primarySelector should be '.seat:focus'.
